briefs.summary: Kirby Yates won in relief and Yohan Ramirez recorded the save; Jeremiah Estrada took the loss in the twelfth as Pittsburgh snapped a three-game slide.

waters.working: Down from 248 a day ago and clearing toward summer low. Pocket-water fishing: a small caddis or stonefly nymph on a long leader through the plunge pools, and a dry along the undercut banks where fish show.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 24.9 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Steady pool stacks fish on structure. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait across the wing dams and the barge-cut seams, early before the sun gets on the water.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 27.3 ft and falling - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Half a foot off on the day but still coloured. Stay on the slack behind rock and the lock wall; a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the riprap until it greens up.

waters.reading: Sound highs 6:39 AM at 3.2 ft and 7:16 PM at 4.0 ft at Hampstead; lows 12:53 AM at 1.0 ft and 12:50 PM at 0.5 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 6:39 AM and 7:16 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The morning high falls to a half-foot low at 12:50 PM - that long ebb is the red drum window, the last of it over the oyster bars and grass edges with finger mullet or shrimp. A 92% waxing gibbous is two nights from full, so spring tides will stiffen the inlet current into the weekend. Water 83.3F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. The Fisherman's Post monthly, published Aug. 3 and three weeks old, has whiting and black drum in the surf on shrimp and sand fleas.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No beach hazards are posted for Topsail this morning per NWS Wilmington.
